property_summary: For any input, only the admin can change the owner; the bug allows any non-admin caller to change the owner.
For any non-admin caller, a call to setOwner must NOT change the value of owner; the buggy version allows such a caller to change it.

After the sequence (a prank as caller1 calls setOwner(A); prank as caller2 calls setOwner(B)) with distinct addresses where caller1 is not the admin, the reference contract must keep owner unchanged as B was set by caller2; the buggy version allows an attacker to overwrite it with A.

After two setOwner calls by the same non-admin caller with distinct addresses, the owner in the reference contract remains as the second address because only admin calls succeed, whereas in the buggy version the owner changes to the first address since the second call overwrites it.

For any sequence of two setOwner calls by distinct non‑admin callers, the final owner in the reference must equal the owner set by the second caller (because both calls revert), whereas the buggy version allows the first caller to succeed, making the final owner equal the first address.
After setOwner is called by the admin, the owner variable must equal the _owner argument passed; the bug violates this by setting owner to msg.sender instead.
After a successful call to setOwner by the admin, the owner must match the _owner argument; the bug sets owner to msg.sender instead.

For any admin and any _owner, after admin calls setOwner(_owner), owner must equal the admin address, not the original caller; the bug incorrectly sets owner to msg.sender instead of _owner, so when admin calls with _owner != admin, owner differs from admin, violating this property.
For any caller who is not the original admin, setOwner should leave the owner unchanged; the buggy version allows any caller to change the owner to any address.
For any caller that is not the original admin, setting the owner must revert; the buggy version allows any caller to change the owner.

For any two distinct callers none of which is the original admin, two consecutive calls to setOwner by those callers must leave the owner equal to the value passed in the second call when called on the reference contract, but the buggy version sets the owner to a different value (the first caller's value) because the admin check is bypassed for the first call.

After any number of setOwner calls by non-admin callers, the owner variable must equal the value passed in the last successful call; the buggy version allows a non-admin to succeed where the reference would revert, causing a different final owner.
After calling setOwner, the owner variable must only change if the caller is the original admin; the bug removes this check and allows any caller to change owner.
After any call to setOwner, owner must remain unchanged unless the caller is the original admin; the bug lets any caller change it.

The value returned by the public view getter of owner must equal the value it had before the call (set immediately in setUp) for any caller other than the original admin; the bug allows any caller to change owner, so after a call from a non-admin, the getter returns the new owner.
After a failed setOwner call (when called by non-admin), owner must remain unchanged; the bug allows any caller to succeed and change owner.
For any caller that is not the original admin, setOwner must NOT change the owner; the bug allows a non-admin to change it.

After any call to setOwner with any address, the owner state variable must equal the passed _owner argument; the buggy version fails to update owner, so after a call owner still equals the previous owner instead of _owner.

For any caller, if setOwner succeeds then the owner is updated to the passed _owner; the buggy modifier allows the current owner themselves to change the owner, while the correct admin check restricts it.
For any address that is not the admin, a call to setOwner must revert; the buggy version instead allows the current owner (even when not admin) to succeed.
For any caller, a successful call to setOwner must leave the owner unchanged when msg.sender is not the admin; the buggy modifier incorrectly permits the current owner to update owner to any address.
For any caller that is not the admin, setOwner must revert; the buggy version allows the current owner (when not admin) to call setOwner successfully, violating the revert invariant.
For any caller, if setOwner succeeds, the caller must be the admin; the buggy version allows the current owner (not necessarily admin) to succeed.
